name: Regular I Jet Boot Left
call: Regular I SL Right 17 Jet Boot
purpose: The change-up to Jet Boot Right. The SL runs the jet the same way, but this time the quarterback keeps it and boots in behind the motion instead of away from it. The end who has been squeezing the keeper the other way is the one it beats.

LTE.rule: Bump the end, then release to the flat at four yards in front of the quarterback.

RTE.rule: Bump the end, then cross to eight yards on the boot side. Late on purpose.

SL.rule: Run the Jet motion for real: full speed, flat across, keep going after the fake. Take the edge defender with you.

QB.rule: Fake the jet, hide it on your back hip, boot left behind the motion. Throw only when they take you.

FB.sell: Fill like Wedge is coming, then take anyone chasing from inside.

TB.sell: Run the Power path left, then protect the outside. Anyone chasing him is yours.

coaching_points: This is the counter to Jet Boot Right — call it once they have started chasing the keeper away from the motion. If nobody has, run the Right one until they do.
Both ends must engage before releasing. If they run straight into their routes the fake dies and the flat defender is already waiting.
No blitzing is allowed for 8- and 9-year-olds, so the quarterback has time. Teach him to be patient and look up.
Run first. At this age the quarterback usually walks into ten yards before anyone finds him.
One throw, then tuck it. No scrambling backwards, ever.
